findings.problem: saveSetting passes a ky-style wrapper: api.put(url, { json: { settings } }). The project's client takes the raw body and JSON.stringifies it, so the request body is {"json":{"settings":...}} while the endpoint binds SettingUpdateRequest requiring a top-level settings key.
findings.impact: Every save fails with 422 before reaching the backend; the entire write path is non-functional in the browser. The store unit test hides it by mocking the api client and asserting the same wrong shape.
findings.recommendation: Pass the body directly: api.put(url, { settings }); fix the test to assert the real shape.

findings.problem: Two defects in _sanitize_markdown. (a) The dangerous-scheme regex runs on the raw string and only matches literal spellings, so [x](javascript:alert(1)) is stored intact and the browser decodes the entity in the href. (b) bleach.clean entity-escapes bare &, < and >, so 'AT&T policy' is persisted as 'AT&T policy'.
findings.impact: (a) The server-side control the acceptance criteria require is bypassable; non-browser consumers of the anonymous GET /v1/config receive a live javascript: link. (b) Any disclaimer containing an ampersand is stored and redisplayed corrupted, including in the truncation tooltip which renders the raw string as text.
findings.recommendation: Canonicalise with html.unescape before the scheme check, and unescape bleach's output before storing so the stored value is the author's Markdown.

findings.problem: list_settings reads through override_cache, the same eventually-consistent per-pod snapshot as the public path, while a write only invalidates the writing pod's cache.
findings.impact: No read-your-writes for the admin on a multi-replica deployment: the refresh after a save can hit another pod, re-render the previous value and badge, and SettingCard's effect then overwrites the admin's typed text with the stale value.
findings.recommendation: Have the admin read path load overrides directly via alist_by_key_prefix; keep the cache for the high-traffic public resolution only.

findings.problem: When a declared component is absent from customer-config.yaml, _resolved_value emits null for every field and resolve_components never applies its override, because it only iterates YAML components.
findings.impact: On any customer deployment whose YAML lacks the declared component the admin page posts nulls and is rejected with 400, and even a stored override would never be served.
findings.recommendation: Fall back to declaration-level defaults in _resolved_value and synthesise a component for a declared id missing from YAML.

findings.problem: The audit event is written in a separate session after the config write has already committed and the cache was invalidated, with no error handling.
findings.impact: An audit-session failure raises out of save_setting, so the client sees a 500 and 'Failed to save' while the override is live and already serving users.
findings.recommendation: Catch and log audit failures so they cannot invert the response of a committed write.

findings.problem: The declarations GET is gated by admin_access_only while the writes use require_customer_config_write. They resolve identically today, but the dedicated dependency exists precisely to be repointed at an RBAC permission later.
findings.impact: The moment the write guard is repointed, read and write diverge and the page loads empty for users who may still write.
findings.recommendation: Gate the declarations GET with require_customer_config_write as well.

findings.problem: useSnapshot(appInfoStore) is called but its result is discarded; the component reads the mutable proxy through appInfoStore.getChatDisclaimer(). valtio only tracks properties accessed on the snapshot, so the component subscribes to nothing.
findings.impact: The disclaimer does not appear when fetchCustomerConfig resolves after first paint and does not update after refetchCustomerConfig; it surfaces only on a reload. Tests miss it because the unit setup mocks valtio without reactivity.
findings.recommendation: Read through the snapshot, e.g. derive the disclaimer from the snapshot's configs.

findings.problem: In handleSave and handleReset only the store call is inside try; the following await refresh() is not.
findings.impact: A refresh failure after a successful write rejects the click handler's promise with no catch, shows neither toast, and leaves a stale value and badge on the card.
findings.recommendation: Move refresh() inside the try, or give it its own catch that still reports success of the write.

findings.problem: The Customer Configuration tab is registered only in the isAdmin branch, but isAdmin and isMaintainer are independent flags and both the API guard and the page admit maintainers.
findings.impact: Half the intended audience can use the feature only by typing the URL; three layers encode three different notions of who may configure.
findings.recommendation: Register the tab for maintainers too, so tab, page guard and API guard agree.

findings.problem: The success toast claims the change reaches all users within a minute, but the frontend caches customer config for the tab lifetime and only the saving admin refetches.
findings.impact: The 60-second guarantee is a pod-level guarantee; for a user with an open tab it is unbounded. The toast asserts something the system does not do for a compliance-relevant setting.
findings.recommendation: Reword the toast to state the guarantee the system actually provides.

findings.problem: Every test that touches the write guard replaces it with a dependency override, so require_customer_config_write's body never executes. test_put_requires_write_permission asserts FastAPI's override plumbing, not the guard.
findings.impact: The only authorisation check protecting runtime mutation of publicly served configuration is untested; a regression that inverts the condition ships green.
findings.recommendation: Test the real dependency against an admin, a maintainer, a project admin and a plain user.

findings.problem: FR-1b requires a declaration to carry length, format and permitted-markup constraints. FieldDeclaration has required, max_length and markup but no format/pattern.
findings.impact: The first key needing a formatted value (URL, slug, colour) cannot be declared without changing the declaration model, the API contract and the frontend validator — the multi-layer change the registry exists to avoid.
findings.recommendation: Add an optional pattern to FieldDeclaration, enforce it on write, surface it in the response model and mirror it in the frontend validator.

findings.problem: resolve_components reimplements the enabled filter and derives the runtime-exclusion set from the ids _get_runtime_config happens to return, whereas get_enabled_components uses set(CONFIG_IDS.values()).
findings.impact: Two copies of the filter can drift; any runtime id omitted conditionally would let a stale YAML component of the same id through on the public endpoint.
findings.recommendation: Derive the exclusion from CONFIG_IDS, as the original does.

rationale: Three lenses ran to completion (blind, edge-case, acceptance); no lens failed, and both diffs were fully readable, so confidence is high. 16 raw findings were deduplicated to 13 blocking ones; the sanitisation defect was reported independently by all of blind and edge-case and is merged into CR-002. Two claims were checked experimentally before being accepted: bleach does not decode character references (the blind lens's stated mechanism was wrong, but the bypass is real via the browser decoding the href), and the ampersand escaping reproduces exactly as reported. CR-001 is the only critical: it makes the entire write path non-functional and was masked by a mock-based test asserting the same wrong call shape. 3 findings were dismissed as style or non-reachable; 0 deferred.
